items.stem:
Read the following case based passage and answer the questions given after passage.

R is an organic compound containing only carbon, chlorine and fluorine. It is produced as a volatile derivative of methane, ethane and propane. It has been widely used as refrigerant, propellent and solvent. Montreal protocol phased out manufacture of such compounds because R contributes to S in the atmosphere.

(i) What is ozone depletion?
(ii) Identify the labelled parts R and S in this passage.
(iii) Which of the following would not be a consequence of S?
(a) Increased rates of lung cancer
(b) Increased incidence of premature skin ageing
(c) Increased incidence of severe sunburns
(d) Increased incidence of cataracts
(iv) Montreal protocol was signed in which year?
(a) 1965
(b) 1987
(c) 2012
(d) 1999
items.answer:
(i) Ozone depletion means the thinning of the ozone layer in the atmosphere. Many chemicals, mainly CFCs, are responsible for it.
(ii) In the given passage, 'R' is chlorofluorocarbon (CFC) and 'S' is ozone depletion.
(iii) (a) Major consequences of ozone depletion are increased incidences of cataracts, severe sunburns, skin cancer and premature ageing of skin etc. UV rays do not affect respiratory organs.
(iv) (b) Montreal protocol was signed on 16 September, 1987.
items.ocr: Section heading is printed as 'CASE BASED QUEATIONS' (sic) in the source; kept as printed. LaTeX $R$ / $S ^ { \prime }$ normalised to plain R and S.

items.stem:
Read the following case based passage and answer the questions given after passage.

Carbon is so versatile in nature that organic chemistry forms a separate branch of chemistry which deals mainly with carbon and its compounds. Carbon is an element with symbol C, atomic number 6 and electronic configuration 2, 4. Carbon has a valency of four. So, it is capable of bonding with four other atoms of carbon or atoms of some other monovalent element. Compounds of carbon are formed with oxygen, nitrogen, hydrogen, sulphur, chlorine and many other elements, giving rise to compounds with specific properties which depend on the elements other than the carbon present in the molecule.

(i) Write the name of the term used for four valency of carbon.
(ii) Name the term used to define property of carbon to form bond with another carbon atom.
(iii) Name the group and period to which carbon belong.
(iv) Which of the following statements is incorrect?
(a) Valence electrons of carbon are 4.
(b) Carbon has a valency of four.
(c) Organic chemistry forms a separate branch of chemistry which deals mainly with carbon and its compounds.
(d) Electronic configuration of carbon is 2, 6.
items.answer:
(i) The term used for four valency of carbon is tetravalency.
(ii) Catenation is the term used to define the property of carbon to form a bond with another carbon atom.
(iii) Carbon belongs to the second period and the fourteenth group of the periodic table.
(iv) (d) Total electrons present in carbon are 6. Out of these 6 electrons, 2 are present in the first shell and the other four in the next shell. This gives the electronic configuration of carbon as 2, 4. Hence, the incorrect option is (d).
items.ocr: The passage is split by the extraction: the number and first half print on page 46 (ending '...compounds with specific properties which'), the tail plus all four sub-questions and the answer key print on page 51. Rejoined here. Printed electronic configuration '- 2 , 4' normalised to '2, 4'. A small unlabelled figure sits between the passage tail and the sub-questions on page 51; no sub-question refers to it, so it is not attached.

items.stem:
Read the following case based passage and answer the questions given after passage.

Ethanol or ethyl alcohol is an important organic compound. It burns in air to form carbon dioxide and water. It is used in industries, hospitals and homes. Ethanol is supplied to hospitals and research laboratories without charging different taxes. Therefore, to prevent its misuse for drinking, it is mixed with some poisonous chemicals. Drinking such an alcohol causes blindness, liver damage and even death.

(i) Based on the data represented in the bar graph given alongside, why is there a reduction in emission of carbon monoxide from vehicles when a mixture of petrol and ethanol was used as fuel?
(ii) Which substance is most commonly added to ethyl alcohol to make it unfit for drinking?
(iii) Which organ in human body is most affected by the excessive intake of alcoholic drinks?
(iv) Ethanol has no effect on litmus solutions. Why?
items.answer:
(i) Ethanol is a clean fuel because it gives only carbon dioxide and water on burning. It does not produce any poisonous gas like carbon monoxide. So, addition of ethanol to petrol has the advantage of reducing the emission of carbon monoxide from vehicles.
(ii) Methyl alcohol (methanol), a poisonous substance, is added to ethyl alcohol to make it unfit for drinking.
(iii) Liver is most affected by the excessive intake of alcoholic drinks.
(iv) Ethanol does not contain any hydrogen ions, so it is a neutral compound. Thus ethanol has no effect on any litmus solution.
items.ocr: Sub-question (i) explicitly refers to 'the bar graph given alongside', so the page-60 figure is attached to the question (not to the solution).

items.stem:
Read the following case based passage and answer the questions given after passage.

A teacher asked Mohan to do the following step under his observation: Take about 3 mL of ethanol in a test tube and warm it gently in a water bath. Add a 5% solution of alkaline potassium permanganate drop by drop to this solution.

(i) Does the colour of potassium permanganate persist when it is added initially?
(ii) Why does the colour of potassium permanganate not disappear when excess is added?
(iii) What happens when ethanol is treated with 5% alkaline solution of KMnO₄?
(iv) What is the colour of potassium permanganate solution?
(v) What is the nature of potassium permanganate?
items.answer:
(i) No. The purple colour due to permanganate gets decolourised during the reaction.
(ii) When all the alcohol gets consumed, the reaction stops and so the purple colour persists.
(iii) Oxidation of ethanol takes place and ethanoic acid is formed.
CH₃CH₂OH + [O] → CH₃COOH (alkaline KMnO₄)
(iv) It is of purple colour.
(v) Potassium permanganate is a powerful oxidizing agent.
items.ocr: MinerU dropped the reaction arrow in the worked solution ('CH₃CH₂OH \frac{[0]}{KMnO₄(alkaline)} * CH₃COOH'); restored as →. LaTeX subscripts rewritten to Unicode.

items.stem:
Read the following case based passage and answer the questions given after passage.

Teacher said to Ganesh to do the following experiment. Take 1 mL ethanol (absolute alcohol) and 1 mL glacial acetic acid along with a few drops of concentrated sulphuric acid in a test tube. Warm in a water-bath for at least five minutes as shown in the figure. Pour into a beaker containing 20–50 mL of water and smell the resulting mixture.

(i) Which one is stronger acid, HCl or ethanoic acid?
(ii) What is glacial acetic acid?
(iii) Name the reaction which takes place between glacial acetic acid and absolute alcohol.
items.answer:
(i) Ethanoic acid is a weaker acid than HCl, as the pH of HCl is less than the pH of ethanoic acid. Hence HCl is the stronger acid.
(ii) 100% pure acetic acid is called glacial acetic acid.
(iii) It is called esterification.
C₂H₅OH + CH₃COOH →(H⁺) CH₃COOC₂H₅ + H₂O
(absolute alcohol + acetic acid → ethyl ethanoate + water)
items.ocr: The question number '300.' and its first sentence print at the very end of page 60 (the last text in the extraction); the experiment text, the figure and all three sub-questions print on page 53. Rejoined here; page recorded as 60, the page the question number and its first sentence print on, as for every other split item in this file. The figure and the three sub-questions print on page 53 and the passage calls the figure out ('as shown in Figure'), so it stays attached. Printed '1 mL 1 glacial acetic acid' corrected to '1 mL glacial acetic acid'.

items.stem:
Read the following case based passage and answer the questions given after passage.

Teacher asked Pawan to carry out the following practical step under his observation: Take about 10 mL of water each in two test tubes. Add a drop of oil (cooking oil) to both the test tubes and label them as A and B. To test tube B, add a few drops of soap solution. Now shake both the test tubes vigorously for the same period of time.

(i) Can you see the oil and water layers separately in both the test tubes immediately after you stop shaking them?
(ii) Leave the test tubes undisturbed for some time and observe. Does the oil layer separate out? In which test tube does this happen first?
(iii) Is oil drop miscible in water?
(iv) Take a test tube. Add a drop of oil in it. Add a piece of soap in it and shake it properly. Would the oil droplets appear again or disappear?
(v) What are soaps?
items.answer:
(i) No, it is not clear.
(ii) In test tube A the oil layer separates out. In test tube A it happens first.
(iii) No, oil drop is not miscible in water.
(iv) Oil droplets disappear, as these are acted upon by soap to form sodium salt of fatty acid (the oil is emulsified inside micelles).
(v) Soaps are sodium salts of fatty acids. Example: C₁₇H₃₅COONa (sodium stearate).
items.ocr: Printed 'Teacher asked to Pawan to carry out following practical step under the observation of him' tidied to readable English. LaTeX C $\mathrm{17}\mathrm{H}_{35}$ COONa rewritten as C₁₇H₃₅COONa.

items.stem:
Read the following case based passage and answer the questions given after passage.

Teacher said to Ganesh to do the following experiment. Take about 10 mL of distilled water (or rain water) and 10 mL of hard water (from a tubewell or hand-pump) in separate test tubes. Add a couple of drops of soap solution to both. Shake the test tubes vigorously for an equal period of time and observe the amount of foam formed.

(i) In which test tube do you get more foam?
(ii) In which test tube do you observe a white curdy precipitate?
(iii) What is hard water?
(iv) Why does soap not form lather with hard water?
(v) Name one pure form of water present in nature.
items.answer:
(i) The test tube containing distilled water has more foam.
(ii) In the test tube containing hard water.
(iii) Water containing soluble salts of Mg²⁺ and Ca²⁺ is called hard water.
(iv) Soap reacts with hard water to form scum and is used up in removing the hardness of the water. So lather is not formed with hard water and soap.
(v) Rain water is the purest form of water found in nature.
items.ocr: LaTeX $\mathrm{Mg^{+2}}$ and $\mathrm{Ca^{+2}}$ rewritten as Mg²⁺ and Ca²⁺.

items.stem:
Read the following case based passage and answer the questions given after passage.

Teacher said to Raheem to do the following experiment: Take two test tubes with about 10 mL of hard water in each. Add five drops of soap solution to one and five drops of detergent solution to the other. Shake both test tubes for the same period.

(i) Do both test tubes have the same amount of foam?
(ii) In which test tube is a curdy solid formed?
(iii) What are detergents?
(iv) Which will form foam with hard water easily, soap or synthetic detergent?
(v) Why is detergent a better cleansing agent than soap?
(vi) Which causes water pollution, detergent or soap?
items.answer:
(i) No, the test tube to which detergent was added has more foam.
(ii) In the test tube in which soap was added.
(iii) Synthetic detergents are sodium salts of a sulphonic acid group (–SO₃Na) attached to a long chain of hydrocarbon.
(iv) Synthetic detergent will form foam more easily with hard water as it does not react with the soluble salts of Mg and Ca present in hard water.
(v) Detergent is a better cleansing agent than soap because detergent acts better even in hard water.
(vi) Detergent causes water pollution, as detergents are non-biodegradable.
items.ocr: LaTeX $\mathrm{(-\ SO_{3}Na)}$ rewritten as (–SO₃Na).

items.stem:
Read the following case based passage and answer the questions given after passage.

The two characteristic features seen in carbon, that is, tetravalency and catenation, put together give rise to many compounds. Many compounds have different atoms or group of atoms attached to different carbon chains.

(i) Draw the structure of the hydrocarbon containing four carbon atoms with single bonds and open chain structure, and with branched chain structure.
(ii) Define catenation.
(iii) Define functional group.
(iv) What are saturated hydrocarbons?
items.answer:
(i) (a) Open chain structure (butane): CH₃–CH₂–CH₂–CH₃
(b) Branched chain structure (2-methylpropane, iso-butane): CH₃–CH(CH₃)–CH₃
(ii) Catenation is the ability of a carbon atom to form bonds with other carbon atoms, linking them into long chains, branched chains and rings.
(iii) A functional group is an atom or group of atoms attached to the carbon chain of an organic compound which determines the properties of that compound.
(iv) Saturated hydrocarbons are those hydrocarbons which contain only carbon–carbon single bonds.
items.ocr: The two printed skeletal structures in the answer key are LaTeX arrays that MinerU mangled (the open chain shows seven C's instead of four); rewritten as condensed formulae for butane and 2-methylpropane, which is what the question asks for.

items.stem:
Read the following case based passage and answer the questions given after passage.

A series of compounds in which the same functional group substitutes for hydrogen in a carbon chain is called a homologous series. Each homologous series has its own general formula. In a given homologous series, there is a gradation in physical properties like melting point and boiling point.

(i) Which functional group is present in the following organic compound?

      H   O
      |   ‖
  H — C — C — H
      |
      H

(ii) Write the general formula of the alkyne homologous series.
(iii) Write the structure of the first member of the alcohol homologous series.
(iv) Which of the following hydrocarbon belongs to the alkene homologous series? C₂H₄, C₃H₄, C₃H₈, C₅H₁₀
items.answer:
(i) The aldehyde (–CHO) functional group is present; the compound is ethanal, CH₃CHO.
(ii) CₙH₂ₙ₋₂ (n ≥ 2)
(iii) The first member is methanol, CH₃OH. Its structure is H₃C–O–H.
(iv) Alkenes have the general formula CₙH₂ₙ. Therefore C₂H₄ and C₅H₁₀ belong to the alkene homologous series.
items.ocr: Sub-part (ii) is printed as 'the general formula of the alkyl in homologous series'; the worked solution gives CₙH₂ₙ₋₂, which is the alkyne series, so 'alkyl' was read as 'alkyne'. Sub-part (iv) and the whole answer key print on page 55 while the stem prints on page 58; rejoined here. Answer key prints 'C₂H₄ and CH₁₀ belongs to alkene'; restored to C₅H₁₀ from the option list. The methanol structure block in the source collapsed to a bare 'H'; restored from the named answer.

items.stem:
Read the following case based passage and answer the questions given after passage.

Ethanol is a liquid at room temperature. Ethanol is commonly called alcohol and is the active ingredient of all alcoholic drinks. It is also used as a solvent in medicines such as tincture of iodine and cough syrup. Ethanol reacts with sodium as well as with carboxylic acids. Ethanol can also undergo dehydration in the presence of sulphuric acid.

(i) What happens when ethanol is strongly heated in the presence of concentrated H₂SO₄?
(ii) Write the chemical equation when ethanol reacts with sodium metal.
(iii) Write the molecular formula of ethanol and draw its structural formula.
(iv) What do you mean by denatured alcohol?
items.answer:
(i) Ethanol forms ethene by dehydration.
CH₃–CH₂OH →(hot and conc. H₂SO₄) CH₂=CH₂ + H₂O
(ii) 2CH₃–CH₂–OH + 2Na → 2CH₃–CH₂ONa + H₂
H₂ gas is evolved.
(iii) Molecular formula: C₂H₅OH. Structural formula: H₃C–CH₂–O–H (each carbon carrying its hydrogens, with the –OH group on the terminal carbon).
(iv) Alcohol which is made unfit for drinking purposes is called denatured alcohol. This is done by adding poisonous substances such as methanol, or by adding copper sulphate to colour it.
items.ocr: Printed '(i) What happens when ethanol a strongly heated' corrected to 'is strongly heated'. LaTeX reaction conditions rewritten with a Unicode arrow; the source had dropped the arrow into a \xrightarrow fraction.

items.stem:
Read the following case based passage and answer the questions given after passage.

Carboxylic acids are a class of organic compounds containing the –COOH functional group. The first member of the carboxylic acid homologous series is formic acid. Carboxylic acids are weak acids, but react with sodium hydroxide, alcohols, metals, etc.

(i) Complete the following equation with the appropriate compound: CH₃COOH + NaHCO₃ →
(ii) Draw the electron dot structure of ethanoic acid.
(iii) Methanoic acid is produced during a bee sting and causes irritation. How will you neutralize this?
(iv) What is esterification?
items.answer:
(i) CH₃COOH + NaHCO₃ → CH₃COONa + H₂O + CO₂
(ii) In the electron dot structure of ethanoic acid (CH₃COOH), the methyl carbon shares one electron pair with each of three hydrogens and one with the carboxyl carbon; the carboxyl carbon shares two pairs with one oxygen (C=O) and one pair with the –O–H oxygen, which in turn shares a pair with hydrogen.
(iii) We neutralize methanoic acid by applying a weak base such as NaHCO₃ (baking soda).
HCOOH + NaHCO₃ → HCOONa + H₂O + CO₂
(iv) Esterification is the reaction of a carboxylic acid with an alcohol in the presence of concentrated sulphuric acid to give a sweet-smelling compound called an ester.
CH₃COOH + CH₃CH₂OH →(conc. H₂SO₄) CH₃COOCH₂CH₃ + H₂O
items.ocr: The electron dot structure printed for answer (ii) is a figure that belongs only to the worked solution, so it is described in words and not attached as an image. Reaction arrows dropped by MinerU were restored from the worked solution.

items.stem:
Read the following case based passage and answer the questions given after passage.

Soaps are sodium or potassium salts of long chain carboxylic acids. The action of soaps and detergents is based on the properties of both hydrophobic and hydrophilic groups in the molecule and this helps to emulsify the oily dirt and hence its removal.

(i) Why can soaps not be used with hard water?
(ii) The cleansing action of soap is due to the formation of clusters called ______.
(iii) Name the process used to prepare soap commercially.
(iv) What is the advantage of soaps over detergents?
items.answer:
(i) Soap molecules react with the magnesium and calcium ions present in hard water to form an insoluble substance called scum.
(ii) Micelles.
(iii) Saponification. On heating with sodium hydroxide, which is an alkali, the vegetable oil or fat (which is an ester) is converted to an alcohol (glycerol) and the sodium salt of a carboxylic acid (called soap).
(iv) Soaps are 100% biodegradable, which means they can be decomposed completely by the bacteria present in water. Hence soaps do not cause water pollution.
items.ocr: The passage and sub-parts (i)–(ii) print at the foot of page 55; sub-parts (iii)–(iv) and the answer key print at the top of page 56. Rejoined. Sub-part (ii) is printed as an unfinished sentence ('...clusters called') and is treated as a fill-in-the-blank within the case study.

(i) Draw the electron dot structure of methanol. (ii) Which of the above compounds does not liberate hydrogen gas on reaction with sodium metal? (iii) Name the compound which gives brisk effervescence on reaction with baking soda. (iv) Which chemical from the above list is added to ethanol to make it unfit for drinking purposes?
items.answer:

(iii) Methanoic acid, HCOOH and ethanoic acid, CH₃COOH.

items.stem:
Read the following case based passage and answer the questions given after passage.
Organic compoundBromineSodiumSodium hydrogen carbonate
EtheneBrown colour disappearsNegativeNegative

(i) Why does ethene decolourize bromine? (ii) Write the chemical equation for the reaction between ethanol and sodium. (iii) Complete the equation: CH₃COOH + NaHCO₃ → (iv) How do you convert ethanol into ethanoic acid? What is this reaction called?
items.answer:
(i) Ethene is an unsaturated hydrocarbon. It decolourizes bromine because bromine adds across the carbon–carbon double bond.
CH₂=CH₂ + Br₂ → CH₂Br–CH₂Br
(ii) 2CH₃CH₂OH + 2Na → 2CH₃CH₂ONa + H₂
(iii) CH₃COOH + NaHCO₃ → CH₃COONa + H₂O + CO₂

CH₃CH₂OH + 2[O] →(acidified K₂Cr₂O₇, heat) CH₃COOH + H₂O
The reaction is called oxidation.

The printed answer to (iv) carries a stray '+ CO₂' from the same scramble; dropped. The bromine-addition equation printed for (i) is only a figure in the source; restored in text. items.stem:
Read the following case based passage and answer the questions given after passage.

Some reactions with organic compounds are given below.
1. 2CH₃CH₂OH + 2Na → 2CH₃CH₂ONa + H₂
2. CH₃CH₂OH →(hot conc. H₂SO₄) CH₂=CH₂ + H₂O
3. CH₃CH₂OH →(alkaline KMnO₄, heat) CH₃COOH
4. CH₃CH₂OH + NaOH → CH₃CH₂ONa + H₂O

(i) Which of the above reactions does not take place?
(ii) Which of the above reactions is a displacement reaction?
(iii) What is the name of CH₃CH₂ONa?
(iv) What type of reaction is the third reaction? What is alkaline KMnO₄ called?
items.answer:
(i) Alcohols do not react with NaOH. Hence reaction (4) does not take place.
(ii) Reaction (1) is a displacement reaction: 2CH₃CH₂OH + 2Na → 2CH₃CH₂ONa + H₂ (sodium displaces the hydrogen of the –OH group).
(iii) Sodium ethoxide.
(iv) Reaction (3) is an oxidation reaction, as there is an addition of oxygen to the starting compound, ethanol. Hot alkaline KMnO₄ is called an oxidizing agent.
items.ocr: Reaction 1 in the printed passage reads '2CH₃CH₂OH + 2Na ⟶ 2CH₃CH₃ONa + H₂' and the printed answer (ii) reads '2CH₂CH₂OH + 2Na 2CH₃CH₂ONa'; both corrected to CH₃CH₂ONa / 2CH₃CH₂OH. A stray '2' floating after reaction 1 was dropped as page furniture. Reaction arrows dropped by MinerU in reactions 2 and 3 were restored.

items.stem:
Read the following case based passage and answer the questions given after passage.

Compounds having carbon atoms among the components are known as carbon compounds. Carbon compounds could only be obtained from a living source; hence they are also known as organic compounds. Bond formed by sharing of electrons is called a covalent bond. Two or more atoms share electrons to make their configuration stable. In this type of bond, all the atoms have similar rights over the shared electrons. Compounds which are formed because of covalent bonds are called 'covalent compounds'. Covalent bonds are of three types: single, double and triple covalent bond. Carbon combines with oxygen, hydrogen, nitrogen, sulphur, chlorine and many other elements to form various stable compounds. The stability of carbon compounds is due to the small size of carbon which enables the nucleus to hold on to the shared pair of electrons strongly. The reactions shown by carbon compounds involve breaking of old bonds in the reacting molecules and the formation of new bonds in the product molecules. Carbon has the unique ability to form bonds with other atoms of carbon, giving rise to large molecules. This property is called catenation.

(i) Which of the following is true about saturated carbon compounds?
(a) Carbon compounds could only be obtained from a living source.
(b) Two or more atoms share electrons to make their configuration.
(c) Carbon giving rise to large molecules.
(d) Atoms are satisfied by forming single covalent bond.
(ii) What is catenation?
(a) It forms bonds with its bond only.
(b) Carbon decreases the molecules.
(c) Existence of an element is 2 or more forms.
(d) Carbon form bonds with other atoms of carbon.
(iii) What is a covalent bond?
(a) Compound contains five carbon atoms.
(b) Undergo substitution reactions with bond.
(c) Electrons shared between atoms to contribute an electron.
(d) Molecule adds on to the multiple bonds.
(iv) What do you mean by isomer?
(a) Atoms have similar rights over shared electrons.
(b) Atoms arising due to electron pair sharing.
(c) Two or more compounds having the same molecular formula.
(d) A three-dimensional structure.
items.answer:
(i) (d) Atoms are satisfied by forming single covalent bond.
(ii) (d) Carbon form bonds with other atoms of carbon.
(iii) (c) Electrons shared between atoms to contribute an electron.
(iv) (c) Two or more compounds having the same molecular formula.
items.ocr: Badly split by the extraction: the passage and only options (a)–(b) of sub-part (i) print at the foot of page 57, while options (c)–(d) of (i) plus all of (ii), (iii), (iv) and the answer key print at the top of page 54. Rejoined here. In sub-part (iv) the option label of choice (c) was lost ('c Two or more compounds...'); restored as (c). Option wording is kept as printed even where it is ungrammatical.

Study the table related to carbon compounds and answer the questions that follow.
General FormulaCnH2nCnH2n−2CnH2n+2
IUPAC name of the homologous seriesAlkeneAlkyneAlkanes
Characteristic bond typeDouble bondTriple bondSingle bond
IUPAC name of the first member of the seriesEtheneEthyneMethane
Type of reaction with chlorineAdditionAdditionSubstitution
(i) Which of the following compound is the next homologue of C₄H₈? (a) C₅H₁₂ (b) C₅H₁₀ (c) C₅H₈ (d) None of these (ii) Write the general formula of butane and hexene. (iii) Write the IUPAC name of the third member of the homologous series of alkynes. (iv) Which of the following compounds will contain a triple bond? (a) C₄H₁₀ (b) C₂H₄ (c) C₂H₆ (d) C₃H₄
items.answer:
(i) (b) C₅H₁₀ (the next homologue in the alkene series CₙH₂ₙ, obtained by adding one –CH₂– unit).
(ii) Butane: C₄H₁₀ (alkane, CₙH₂ₙ₊₂); hexene: C₆H₁₂ (alkene, CₙH₂ₙ).
(iii) Propyne, CH₃–C≡CH.
(iv) (d) C₃H₄, which is propyne, H₃C–C≡C–H, and contains a carbon–carbon triple bond.

items.stem:
Read the following case based passage and answer the questions given after passage.

In diamond, each carbon atom is bonded to four other carbon atoms by a single covalent bond. This is why a diamond is a rigid, compact, three dimensional structure and is very hard to break. It is a bad conductor of heat and electricity, as there are no free electrons present in it. On the other hand graphite contains free electrons, so it is a good conductor of heat and electricity. Lead pencils contain graphite encased in a wooden covering. A fullerene molecule consists of 60 carbon atoms arranged in pentagons and hexagons, like in a standard football. In carbon compounds, different compounds are formed with different structures with the same molecular formula. These compounds are called isomers and the phenomenon is called 'isomerism'. Carbon compounds in which all the four valencies of carbon atom are satisfied by forming single covalent bonds are known as saturated carbon compounds.

(i) Discuss why a diamond is a rigid, compact, three dimensional structure and is very hard to break.
(ii) What are saturated carbon compounds?
items.answer:
(i) In diamond each carbon atom is bonded to four other carbon atoms by strong single covalent bonds, forming a continuous three dimensional network. This rigid, compact giant structure is what makes diamond very hard and difficult to break.
(ii) Carbon compounds in which all the four valencies of the carbon atom are satisfied by forming single covalent bonds are called saturated carbon compounds.
items.ocr: The passage prints at the foot of page 54 and the two sub-questions with their answer key print at the top of page 59; rejoined. Only two sub-parts are printed for this case study.

Study the table which shows some information about four organic compounds A, B, C and D and answer the questions that follow.
Organic compoundMolecular formulaMelting point (C)Boiling point (C)
AC3H8188− 42
BC4H101381
CC5H1213036
DCH12680
(i) Which of these organic compounds belong to the alkane series? (ii) Based on the information given above, state one characteristic of the alkane series. (iii) The homologous series C₆H₁₂ belongs to (a) alkane (b) alkene (c) alkyne (d) none of these (iv) The IUPAC name of the compound having molecular formula C₄H₁₀ is (a) methane (b) butane (c) propane (d) ethane
items.answer:
(i) C₃H₈, C₄H₁₀ and C₅H₁₂ all have the general formula CₙH₂ₙ₊₂, so all of these (A, B and C) belong to the alkanes.
(ii) They have the general formula CₙH₂ₙ₊₂ and their melting points and boiling points increase with increase in molecular mass.
(iii) (b) As C₆H₁₂ has the general formula CₙH₂ₙ, it belongs to the alkene series.
(iv) (b) Butane.

In sub-part (iv) the option label (a) was lost ('is methane (b) butane...'); restored from position. Answer (i) printed 'j₄H₁₀' for C₄H₁₀; repaired.

items.stem:
Answer the following questions based on hydrocarbons and their conversions.

(i) Draw the structure of the hydrocarbon with general formula CₙH₂ₙ₋₂ where n = 3.
(ii) Which reaction is used to convert unsaturated hydrocarbons to saturated hydrocarbons?
(iii) Name the catalyst used in the above conversion reaction.
(iv) Select the alkenes and the alkynes from the following: C₂H₄, C₃H₄, C₂H₂, C₄H₈
items.answer:
(i) For n = 3, CₙH₂ₙ₋₂ gives C₃H₄, which is propyne. Its structure is H₃C–C≡C–H.
(ii) Hydrogenation reaction (an addition reaction).
(iii) Nickel catalyst (finely divided nickel, at about 573 K).
(iv) C₂H₄ and C₄H₈ are alkenes; C₃H₄ and C₂H₂ are alkynes.

Answer (i) LaTeX shows 'H-C-C≡C-H' with stray H's; rewritten as H₃C-C≡C-H.
